messages:
Alex Kim: Customer report — our assistant invoked the wrong tool and charged the customer instead of issuing a refund. Customer C-4489 hit us with an angry email. Payload they sent below (sanitized):
```
{
  "user_id": "C-4489",
  "text": "I want a refund for order 9876",
  "amount": 25.00
}
```
Can someone take a look?

SupportBot: Escalation created and pinged #eng-oncall and #sre-oncall :rotating_light:

Priya Rao: Do we have the model/tool trace? Was it a router mis-choice or did `charge_customer` accept the args and execute? :thinking:

Alex Kim: Pasting sanitized model trace — it chose `charge_customer` with these args:
```
tool_choice: charge_customer
args: { "customer_id": "C-4489", "amount": 25.00, "currency": "USD" }
model_confidence: 0.76
```
Router logs show the tool selection happened before validation.

Jordan S: Oncall checking quickly. Router ranking uses name/alias matching + LM score. Possible ambiguity between `create_refund` and `charge_customer` when user phrasing is short. Running a quick grep on router traces now.
`curl -s "${ROUTER_LOG_API}/traces?trace_id=1844561234"`

SRE Oncall: I fetched the trace. The model produced candidates for both `charge_customer` and `create_refund`. The router picked `charge_customer` because the LM score for its signature tokens was higher. Post-selection we did not block execution with a stricter schema check — `charge_customer` happily accepted amount and proceeded.
Immediate mitigation: add a prompt-level disambiguation step when intent contains "refund"/"return" that asks the model to confirm tool intent, and add a schema guard that rejects `charge_customer` calls missing `charge_authorization` and `charge_reason`.

Maria Patel: Customer already got charged. We need to issue a manual refund and update the ticket SR-12345. Billing requires `refund_reason` field when processed manual. Can someone run the admin refund tool and confirm?

Jordan S: I'll run the manual refund now and roll a hotfix to the router metadata. Manual steps I ran:
```
# admin tool (internal)
POST /internal/admin/refund
{ "order_id": 9876, "amount": 25.00, "reason": "mistaken charge via assistant" }
```
Refund processed — refund id R-7721. Updating SR-12345.
I've pushed a hotfix to tool router metadata: added aliases for `create_refund` = ["refund","return","issue refund","refund request"] and added a pre-exec schema validation that `charge_customer` requires `authorization_token` and `charge_reason`. If those keys are missing, router will prefer `create_refund` when user text contains refund/return synonyms.
Rolling to canary 10% now. Monitoring logs. :rocket:

Alex Kim: QA/repro notes — to reproduce locally: call the assistant with prompt: "I want a refund for order 9876" and check `router.trace.candidates`. If `charge_customer` shows up with higher score we have regression. I'll attach a sample curl for QA: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/assist -d '{"user_id":"C-4489","text":"I want a refund for order 9876","amount":25}'
```

Jordan S: Also added an integration unit test in router-tests: test_tool_choice_refund_vs_charge that feeds several refund-like prompts and asserts selected_tool == `create_refund`. Will add eval hooks to alert when tool_choice flips for a high-volume prompt set.

SupportBot: Ticket SR-12345 updated — status: customer_refunded, internal_note: hotfix rolled to canary, monitor in progress. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SR-12345

Priya Rao: Good catch everyone. Postmortem if this happens again, but action items: (1) confirm hotfix to 100% after canary stability, (2) add schema guard for destructive tools, (3) add prompt disambiguation, (4) add evals/alerts. I'll own the follow-up and schedule a quick sync tomorrow. :+1:

Maria Patel: Thanks — please cc me when refund visible to customer. I'll send a soft apology and refund confirmation.

Alex Kim: Closing loop here once canary hits 100% and SR-12345 is resolved. Thanks all.
